newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms, spreads stable in slow talk.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms, spreads stable in slow talk.

text.p: European gas oil firmed in line with stronger futures on Thursday but cargo differentials were broadly unchanged in slow discussion, traders said.
September IPE gas oil gained $3.75 a tonne to $173.75, reflecting strength in U.S. gasoline and catching up with a late rally on Brent crude futures on Wednesday.

Barge premiums on the ARA market were difficult to call due to morning gains in futures. Rotterdam refinery heating oil was called around September IPE flat to -25 cents after a couple of early morning trades at September flat fob ARA.
But bids and offers bounced around in late morning in a very thin market.

"Most people are keeping out of the market because of the screen movement," a trader in Amsterdam said. Rotterdam refinery grade low sulphur diesel was bid around September +$4 with notional offers of around $4.50.
On cargoes, heating oil was September IPE +$0.50/$1.00 cif NWE. Low sulphur diesel was seen around +$4.50/$5.50 cif NWE.
In the Med, Syria was due to issue a tender for gas oil. Traders were discussing EN590 trade at around September +$1.50, the level of a Lavera trade on Wednesday.
